name: html-coding
when_to_use: When authoring, structuring, inspecting, debugging, or validating HTML documents and static web markup, including semantic structure, forms, tables, and accessibility.
steps: Phase 1 — Inspection: Read any existing HTML file and identify the doctype, lang attribute, head/meta structure, character encoding, and overall nesting before editing.

Phase 2 — Implementation: Author well-formed HTML5 using the right element for the right job (POSH). Include <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="...">, <head> with <meta charset="utf-8"> and viewport, a descriptive <title>, and semantic landmarks (header, nav, main, section, article, aside, footer) over generic <div> containers.

Phase 3 — Semantics: Use native elements for their purpose — <button> for actions, <a href> for navigation, <ul>/<ol> for lists, <h1>–<h6> in a logical single hierarchy, <table> only for tabular data. Never simulate headings with <span> styling or buttons with styled <div>.
Phase 4 — Accessibility: Add meaningful alt text to (empty alt="" for purely decorative images), associate every form control with a

Phase 5 — Validation & Verification: Confirm all tags are properly nested and closed, verify the document parses, run a validator when possible (W3C Markup Validation Service or tidy), and preview visually via browser or a local server (e.g. python -m http.server).
Output Rule: After writing an HTML file, reply in 1-4 concise plain-text lines in third person stating what was created and any unverified rendering, without dumping the full source.
verification: read_file confirms the HTML document has a doctype, matching open/close tags, and valid nesting
document parses without obvious structural errors (optional: tidy -eq or W3C validator)
images carry alt attributes, form controls carry associated labels, tables use th scope and caption
